scope: Proposition 13.3 (Ring-class characters with prescribed local values) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 100. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix finitely many split primes of K above odd rational primes, outside 2N, and orient one prime in each conjugate pair. There are distinct split rational primes ri avoiding all the fixed data and characters ξi : Gal(Hri /K) −→ Z/2ni Z, ni −→ ∞, such that ξi is surjective on the inertia quotient at ri, is zero at the primes above 2N, and has odd value at each prescribed oriented prime. We can require ri → 1 in Z2 and v2(2 + ari (E)), v2(2 − ari (E)), v2 det(1 ± Frri | T) ≤ cE. (13.3) The constant cE is independent of the list and of K.
